coverage.r1: Holes: 15:43-16:52 Medi lines are '[speaking foreign language]' (Arabic not transcribed). 04:33-05:00 Medi talks to house staff in English. 03:10-15:41 and 19:51-21:16 mostly English meta talk about the app; Amal's 12:39-15:41 lines are engine MSA translations of her English. Engine writes أديب for قريب (47:11-47:41, both speakers); 42:00 Amal 'وين القلب؟ وين بنحط القلب؟' is likely the engine for 'where do we put el-'. 42:20 'ولاد إمي' vs عمي is a dropped ع (S4), not scored. 1:00:39 'جنين؟' = he misheard جمع (Jenin, name) - listening confusion, not scored. 10:43-10:52 'بطفة/بنفع' unclear example word, skipped. Self-fixes not written: 16:19 بسطت -> انبسطت (before Amal's إنبسطت 16:44), 28:34 ما تشتغلي -> ما بتشتغل, 29:42 تشتـ -> بتشتغل, 43:18 كبير -> كبيرة, 1:02:25 بيروحوا -> بيروح, 56:47 تلاتة -> تلاتاش. Questions not written: 18:24 أكتر إشي وزن or أكتر وزن, 31:50 مهندس الأستاذ?, 39:48 plural here?, 51:10 حفدين/حفيدين, 53:29 اسمه or اسمها. Echo candidates: all six are real English (you know / Tell you about / There's no M? / Uh / Okay / Bye) - no echo fixes. No tier-3 rows: English words used (pounds, venture capital, AI, Utah) are not on her sheet. 44:53 'اثناش بنات' not written: her chat types 'etna3sh banaat'.
coverage.r2: 00:00-16:00 is almost all English (app/AI talk, Medi on the phone 04:33-05:00 and 06:38-07:30); 12:39-15:41 Amal lines are engine-translated MSA of her English, not her words. 16:19 بسطت -> انبسطت is his own self-fix before her 16:44 إنبسطت (GR-22, not written). 28:38 ما بتشتغل overlaps her بتشتغل (written low). 42:00 Amal 'وين القلب؟ وين بنحط القلب؟' is most likely the engine for 'وين ال؟ وين بنحط ال؟' (where do we put el-). 42:20 ولاد إمي = he said 3ammi with the ع dropped (S4), Amal queried 'My mom', not written. 47:11-47:34 أديب = engine for قريب (2areeb) in both voices. 1:00:39/1:00:43 جنين = he misheard her جمع (listening), a name, not written. 1:02:25 بيروحوا -> بيروح self-fixed before her. 1:03:41 'ضل إشي' = one more left, not a correction. Echo candidates for this date (you know / Tell you about / There's no M?) are real English, no echo fixes.

r3_note: Several D-rows are hunts for a quizzed word where Medi said 'I forgot' (relatives, siblings) - ruled tier 0 didn't-know. 54:01 'between twenty and seventeen' is a content range (17-20), not a language slip. 49:43 مرات was self-fixed to مرة at 49:45 before any help. Agreed rows A18 and A34 challenged (self-fix / ambiguous بيدرس).

rows.amal_said: What's the better word؟ ... No. ... The third one. ... Close.
rows.chat: shu ra2yek = what do you think?
rows.why: He used بتظني (you suppose) then بتفكري and قصدك for 'what do you think'; Amal said 'What's the better word', 'No' each time until he reached شو رأيك (sheet: what do you think? | Shu ra2yak).

rows.medi_said: أنا حملت؟ حملت؟ um الأكثر الأكثر إشي
rows.amal_said: نعم، عادي، حملت. بس، وزن is weight، وزن.
rows.why: He said 'I don't know how to say... I lifted the most amount ever'; Amal supplied وزن (weight) - a didn't-know.

rows.medi_said: أنا حملت؟ حملت؟ um الأكثر الأكثر إشي
rows.amal_said: we would need biggest. So, would be أكبر، أكبر وزن ... ممكن، we can use أكثر ... أكثر وزن.
rows.why: Comparative/superlative takes no el- and goes before the noun; Amal recast as أكبر وزن / أكتر وزن.

rows.medi_said: Is it مي- uh, مئين؟ مئين؟ مئين؟
rows.amal_said: No. ميا. Let's go to ميا first. Is ميا feminine؟ ... So what do we do to dual form؟
rows.why: Two hundred is the dual of feminine ميا (ميتين); Amal said No and walked him to the dual, he then said ميتين.

rows.amal_said: لا. ... What's above؟ ... It sounds like صوت بس مش o sound.
rows.why: He used على for 'above / up to'; Amal said لا and hinted until he found فوق (sheet: up / above | Foaq).
rows.english: from the ground to above (my head)

rows.medi_said: Is it محرك or it's حركة؟
rows.why: He asked which word means 'movement'; Amal answered حركة - a didn't-know.
Feminine حركة takes feminine واحدة after it; Amal recast immediately.
Feminine مرة needs واحدة; Amal recast and he repeated it.

rows.amal_said: بعد. What do we put after بعد؟ ... ما.
rows.chat: 3ashaan ba3ed ma a7mel foa2 raasi barajj3o
rows.why: After ba3ed it is ba3ed ma + bare verb (no b-); Amal prompted and he produced ما أحمل.

rows.medi_said: أنا حطيت أرجع؟ Is that right? حطيت أرجع، No?
rows.chat: 3ashaan ba3ed ma a7mel foa2 raasi barajj3o
rows.why: For 'I put it back' he used the plain verb أرجع (I go back) after حطيت; the fix is the doubled-middle causative barajj3o (I return it) - B12 make-X vs get-X; Amal said No and gave برجع.
rows.english: (after lifting it over my head) I put it back down
rows.r3_why: Both readers saw the same slip; the fix is raje3 -> rajja3 (doubled middle = make-X), which the brief files as B12 grammar, not vocab.

rows.why: حدا means 'someone', not 'people'; Amal asked 'what is people?' and he answered الأشخاص, she confirmed ناس، أشخاص (sheet: people | Naas, person | Sha5s).
Asked for 'jobs' he gave the verb 'I work'; Amal said No and asked for the plural of شغل.
Asked the plural of شغل he invented شغلين / شغلات; Amal said No, he then reached أشغال and she said Yes - an invented plural pattern of a word he knows (tier 2 per the brief).
rows.r3_why: Real: explicit No to his invented plural; a distinct wrong piece from A11 (بشتغل) in the same prompt. Labelled vocab-A tier 2 as the brief names 'wrong plural pattern he invented' as tier 2.

rows.medi_said: أبوي في المحل السجاد. في محل
rows.chat: ana bashte8el ma3 abuy fi ma7al el-sajjaad
rows.why: First word of an idafa takes no el-; he said المحل السجاد, started 'في محل' and Amal finished the recast في محل السجاد, which he repeated.

rows.medi_said: ما تشتغلي، ما بتشتغلي، بس ما بتشتغل
rows.why: For 'my mom doesn't work' he said ما تشتغلي / ما بتشتغلي (you-fem ending); Amal said بتشتغل at 28:38, the same second his line 'بس ما بتشتغل' starts (بس first), and he repeated ما بتشتغل at 28:40 - her word likely came before his, but it may be his own self-fix.
rows.r3_why: Her word and his fixed word land in the same second; his line opens with بس so her بتشتغل likely precedes his (GR-24), and he repeats it after her. Kept low.

rows.medi_said: آ أخوي مع-- uh not with ... yeah، في ... بناته.
rows.chat: bas heyye betsaa3ed a5uy fi banaato
rows.why: saa3ad takes fi for 'help with'; he knew مع was off but had no replacement until Amal said 'in' and he said في.
rows.english: she helps my brother with his daughters

rows.medi_said: وأخوي آآ مح-- أخوي محمي، or محم؟ محمي
rows.amal_said: محامي. ... محامي. It's long and it's not doubled.
rows.why: He was unsure of the shape of 'lawyer' (محمي / محم, and محمد at 29:22) and Amal recast محامي twice, explaining the long aa (sheet: lawyer | Mu7aami | محامي); محمي is a different word (protected). May be judged F2 vowel length instead.
rows.english: and my brother is a lawyer
rows.r3_why: Amal voiced the fix twice and he kept missing it (محمد) - more than a sound slip; wrong form of a sheet word, kept as vocab-A tier 2 with a note that it may be F2.

rows.medi_said: what was the plural for عمو؟
rows.why: He asked for the plural; Amal hinted with the abwaab pattern and he found أعمام (didn't-know).
Masculine مهندس (his uncle) takes واحد; he had said واحدة at 30:48 too, Amal recast واحد.

rows.amal_said: Why how do you say the other? Or the second? Mm-hmm. The.
rows.why: 'The other one' is el-taani; Amal prompted 'The.' and he said التاني.

rows.amal_said: أستاذ هندسة. We would use the noun here. أستاذ هندسة.
rows.why: Profession idafa takes the field noun (هندسة), not the person noun; Amal said 'we would use the noun here'.

rows.medi_said: Uh الآخر واحدة. or الـ الـ آخر الواحدة. آخر واحد
rows.amal_said: Where do I put the ل؟ ... Actually we never put ل. آخر واحد. ... Because if we put ل what does it mean?
rows.why: aa5er + noun = last, never el- in front (el- makes 'the end of'); Amal named the rule; he kept saying الواحد / واحدة after.
rows.r3_challenge: Self-fix in the same turn (GR-22): his 32:18 line ends with آخر واحد before Amal's 'Where do I put the ل?'; her reply only explains the rule (though he wavered to الواحد at 32:33).

My reading: كلياً means 'totally / entirely', not 'in total'; he meant 'in total I have five female cousins'; Amal let it pass.
